# Phase 14 gate report: the ladder on LongBench, real long-document question answering

**Status: complete. The gate deliverables are done (tests, experiment, this report, commit).**

Everything through Phase 13 is synthetic: needles, RULER chains and book perplexity. LongBench v1
(arXiv 2308.14508) asks questions about Wikipedia passages, papers and reports at their natural
length, scored by token F1. It is the brief's fourth quality measure (§B7.4, "a couple of LongBench
subsets if time allows"). Phases 12-13 found Quest-style selection losing multi-hop chains at the
tightest budget, so the subsets chosen were LongBench's multi-document, multi-hop QA (HotpotQA,
2WikiMQA, MuSiQue), with single-document QA (MultiFieldQA-en) as the in-run control.

## Gate checklist (CLAUDE.md rule 3)

- [x] **Tests run.** `pytest`, all passing. New: `tests/test_longbench.py` (F1 as LongBench computes
  it, maximum over reference answers, middle truncation that keeps both the instruction and the
  question) and `tests/test_phase14_analysis.py` (a task below the floor is excluded, pairing uses
  only prompts both conditions answered). The transcribed prompts, generation lengths and F1 were
  also checked byte for byte against the reference repository's files before any run.
- [x] **Real experiment run.** `scripts/05_longbench.py --config configs/phase14.yaml`, detached
  from a worktree pinned at the commit under test.
- [x] **Phase doc written.** This file.
- [x] **Committed and pushed.**

## What was measured

Prompts, truncation, generation lengths and scoring follow the LongBench reference code at commit
`2e00731`, on the official data release. Every task takes the first
50 prompts in file order that are at
least 4,096 tokens long; that length rule was added after a two-prompt smoke test showed a 6.25%
budget of a 2K-token prompt is smaller than a window policy's minimum, and before the run. Prompts
ran 4,191–16,432
tokens, and 0 needed truncation. Rungs 2, 4
and 5 at every budget. The 100% block-pool control matched the full cache on every prompt.

| Task | Role | Prompts | Full-cache F1 | Clears the 15 F1 floor |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 2wikimqa | multi-hop | 50 | 25.6 | yes |
| hotpotqa | multi-hop | 50 | 35.5 | yes |
| multifieldqa_en | control | 50 | 38.5 | yes |
| musique | multi-hop | 50 | 21.1 | yes |

Every task cleared the floor, fixed in the config before the run, so all four are analyzed.

## 1. The answer: no multi-hop shortfall detected, at intervals too wide to exclude one

Pooled multi-hop retention (HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA and MuSiQue together) beside the single-document
control, per rung and budget, with both of Phase 12's tests:

| Policy | Budget | Single-doc retention | 95% CI | Multi-hop retention | 95% CI | Disjoint-CI test | Difference CI |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| H2O-style (rung 4) | 75% | 95.6% | 87.4–103.2% | 96.5% | 89.8–101.5% | overlapping | -8.9 to +10.5 pp |
| H2O-style (rung 4) | 50% | 91.9% | 82.6–100.5% | 93.3% | 85.6–99.6% | overlapping | -10.5 to +12.3 pp |
| H2O-style (rung 4) | 25% | 90.6% | 78.1–103.1% | 85.8% | 75.5–95.2% | overlapping | -21.1 to +10.7 pp |

| H2O-style (rung 4) | 6.25% | 79.6% | 61.7–101.4% | 71.0% | 57.8–83.7% | overlapping | -34.1 to +13.3 pp |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 75% | 100.8% | 95.7–105.4% | 100.5% | 100.0–101.6% | overlapping | -5.1 to +4.8 pp |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 50% | 94.8% | 87.0–102.3% | 100.3% | 98.6–102.1% | overlapping | -2.4 to +13.3 pp |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 25% | 90.9% | 80.8–101.0% | 95.1% | 87.5–101.2% | overlapping | -8.6 to +16.1 pp |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 12.5% | 90.5% | 77.3–104.4% | 91.1% | 79.9–101.1% | overlapping | -17.0 to +17.1 pp |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 6.25% | 78.6% | 64.6–94.3% | 77.2% | 65.4–88.1% | overlapping | -21.1 to +16.6 pp |
| Window + sink (rung 2) | 75% | 76.4% | 63.3–89.8% | 85.8% | 75.0–95.1% | overlapping | -7.6 to +25.1 pp |
| Window + sink (rung 2) | 50% | 74.6% | 61.8–88.0% | 85.8% | 74.3–96.6% | overlapping | -6.3 to +27.9 pp |
| Window + sink (rung 2) | 25% | 72.2% | 60.5–85.3% | 76.2% | 63.7–88.0% | overlapping | -13.7 to +20.7 pp |
| Window + sink (rung 2) | 12.5% | 74.3% | 59.5–90.4% | 68.7% | 56.0–81.2% | overlapping | -25.8 to +13.4 pp |
| Window + sink (rung 2) | 6.25% | 64.9% | 50.8–81.9% | 64.7% | 51.9–77.6% | overlapping | -21.4 to +18.9 pp |

**No cell separates, under either test.** At the tightest budget Quest-style selection retains
77.2% of the full cache's F1 on multi-hop
QA and 78.6% on the control. The RULER
shortfall Phase 13 established at this budget does not reappear here.

**That is "not detected", not "absent".** The difference interval at that budget runs from
-21.1 pp to
+16.6 pp, which contains the gap Phase 13
measured on variable tracking
(-19.8 pp). With
50 prompts per task and F1's partial
credit, this phase cannot see an effect of that size. One reading consistent with both phases:
if LongBench's multi-hop questions name the entities they are about, a query-aware selector can see
what it needs from the question alone, which RULER's variable tracking was built to prevent. Neither
the premise nor the reading is checked here.

**Every rung loses much less here than on needles.** The window with a sink at 25% retains
72.2% of the control's F1 and
76.2% of multi-hop F1, against
24.4% of NIAH retrieval at
the same budget on the ladder. The
contexts are shorter (at most 16,432 tokens against the
ladder's 32K) and F1 gives partial credit, so this is not a like-for-like comparison, but it is the
direction every earlier phase would predict: needle retrieval is the harshest test a residency
policy faces.

**The ladder's order mostly holds.** Below 75%, Quest-style selection retains at least as much as
H2O-style eviction, which retains at least as much as the window, in every budget-and-group cell but
one: on the control at 6.25%, H2O-style eviction
(79.6%) edges Quest-style selection
(78.6%). These are point estimates; the
rung-to-rung differences were not tested.

## 2. What this changes

- **§B7.4 is measured.** Four LongBench QA subsets, every budget, rungs 2, 4 and 5.
- **The multi-hop qualifier stays scoped to RULER.** FINDINGS says Quest-style selection's lead
  holds "for retrieval the query can see"; real multi-hop QA did not break it at this sample size.
- **Needle retrieval remains the study's hardest and most discriminating quality test**, which
  supports keeping it as the headline.
